description: A long-form B2B/technical article about a structured 4-day onboarding rollout, sourced from an internal engineering-team retrospective.

endorsedOutput.title: How We Cut Onboarding Time in Half With a Structured 4-Day Rollout
endorsedOutput.excerpt: A breakdown of the onboarding changes that actually moved the needle for our engineering team, and the one metric that mattered most.
endorsedOutput.bodyMarkdown:
## The problem with our old onboarding

New engineers took nearly a month before they shipped their first meaningful change. Most of that time wasn't spent learning the codebase — it was spent figuring out who to ask and where things lived.

## What we actually changed

We restructured the first week into four fixed days: environment setup, a guided codebase walkthrough with a paired engineer, a small scoped ticket, and a review session with the whole team. Nothing changed about the technical content — the structure was the change.

## The results after one quarter

Across the twelve engineers who went through the new process, median time to first merged pull request dropped 47% [1], from 19 days to about 10. Retention at the 90-day mark also held steady, which mattered as much to us as the speed.

## What we'd do differently

The biggest gap was documentation for the paired-engineer sessions — two people ran it differently in ways new hires noticed. If you're trying this, write the walkthrough script down before your first cohort, not after.

If your team is rethinking its own onboarding, a structured first week is worth testing before you assume the problem is your documentation.
